claim: For every open convex neighborhood Omega of zero in finite-dimensional physical space, Laplace-transform interior cone positivity on Omega is equivalent to existence of a smooth everywhere positive strictly log-concave scalar regularizer with full finite exponential-moment domain exactly Omega and positive regularized compact distribution.

scope.cone: proper closed convex cone with nonempty interior; pointedness unnecessary
scope.input: compactly supported distribution of arbitrary finite order, with interior cone-valued total mass
scope.domain: open convex neighborhood of zero; may be unbounded, nonsymmetric, nonsmooth, or contain lines
scope.regularizer: C-infinity, strictly positive, pointwise positive-definite negative-log Hessian
scope.weighted_integrability: all regularizer derivatives and all output derivatives in norm, uniformly weighted by support functions of compact subsets of Omega
scope.symmetry: regularizer may inherit every orthogonal symmetry of Omega; in particular radial for centered balls and R^m

construction: explicit lower-dimensional polar reciprocal-power convex exhaustion
positive globally 1-Lipschitz minorant of normalized cone margin
scalar envelope prescribing an arbitrarily large dual Hessian
convex conjugation giving small Hessian in gradient coordinates
fixed compact mollification controlling all required higher jets
exact retained-tilt distributional remainder and cone sandwich
Fenchel lower bounds for interior moments and separating-cylinder divergence for every exterior or boundary tilt

explicit_extension_example.density: p proportional to sech(lambda*x_1) times a Gaussian in the other coordinates
explicit_extension_example.global_obstruction: H is negative outside the slab, so no noise with all exponential moments can regularize positively

cross_audit.verdict: No mathematical gap found at the stated scope; actual steps audited separately; worker agreement is not proof. Root finite-ball statement should retain proper-cone source hypothesis or handle trivial C=E separately.

limits: No historical priority or exceptional breakthrough claim
No efficient oracle access to compact positivity margins
No useful variance, sampling, precision, or physical resource bound
Radiality cannot be retained for a nonball exact open moment domain
Uniform strong log-concavity is incompatible with a proper finite-moment domain
The output may have a larger moment domain than the scalar noise through cancellation
